summary: Reviewed where Calder's deal flow comes from and agreed to shift the mix toward proprietary origination over 18 months. Agreed a direct approach programme to founders aged 55 and over in the three priority sectors from week 1. Founder dinners depend on budget and the website was parked.

discussion.keyPoints: Helen's data from week 1 showed about 85% of qualified opportunities come from advisers and 15% are proprietary. Mark said the team screens around 300 teasers a year and most are a poor fit.
Mark is willing to give one associate time to run founder outreach. Helen was concerned about cutting across advisers who might feel Calder is going around them.
Helen likes the idea of small founder dinners but has no events budget signed off for next year.

recommendations.recommendation: Move from 85/15 to 60% adviser-led and 40% proprietary origination over the next 18 months.
Run a direct approach programme to 150 named founders aged 55 and over in the priority sectors, at 10 new approaches a week, run by a Calder associate.
Host two founder dinners a year, one in Leeds and one in Newcastle, with 12 founders at each.
Screen fewer but better opportunities: target 120 qualified opportunities a year rather than reading 300 unqualified teasers.
Rebuild the website with a dedicated page for founders thinking about a sale.

actions.action: Build the list of 150 founders aged 55 and over from Companies House and sector data

nextFocus: Tighten how the deal team runs first meetings and qualifies opportunities.
nextPreparation: Bring the current first meeting notes template and the IC screening paper.

tests.question: What origination mix are we aiming for?
How many founders are in the direct approach programme?
